antidotes.why: Do not push yourself down or hold yourself in contempt.

antidotes.source: Vyadha Gita; MBh Shanti 7; Yoga Vasishtha
antidotes.why: Resolve frees from repeating the deed that regret frees from.
The texts send a voice that lifts the shame: you torment yourself for nothing.
Turning from great wrong counts as good because surrender answers self-blame.
It was never all your doing.

chains.summary: Hanuman, after burning Lanka, said that those who put out rising anger with good sense are blessed, as fire is put out with water. In anger a person cannot tell what should and should not be said or done. Carried away, he said he may have destroyed the very one he came to save.
chains.title: What anger made me do

verses.m: An angry person never knows what should and should not be said. For the angry, nothing is off limits to do or to say.
verses.sa: वाच्यावाच्यं प्रकुपितो न विजानाति कर्हिचित्। नाकार्यमस्ति क्रुद्धस्य नावाच्यं विद्यते क्वचित्॥

chains.summary: By regret one is freed from the wrong done. By resolving I will not do it again one is freed from repeating it. Turning to good after a wrong, one comes out like the moon from behind a cloud.
chains.title: Regret, then resolve

verses.m: One who feels remorse for a wrong deed is freed from that wrong; by resolving 'I will not do it again', he is freed from the second.
verses.sa: विकर्मणा तप्यमानः पापाद्विपरिमुच्यते / न तत्कुर्यां पुनरिति द्वितीयात्परिमुच्यते

verses.m: If a person who has done wrong turns to doing good, he is freed from all his wrongs, like the moon coming out from behind a great cloud.
verses.sa: पापं चेत्पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते / मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महाभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः

depicts.m: Whether a task is good or bad, a wise person should first carefully weigh its outcome. The result of deeds done in great haste burns the heart like a thorn until one's dying day.
depicts.sa: गुणवदगुणवद्वा कुर्वता कार्यजातं परिणतिरवधार्या यत्नतः पण्डितेन । अतिरभसकृतानां कर्मणामाविपत्ते- र्भवति हृदयदाही शल्यतुल्यो विपाकः ॥
depicts.why: Shows the lodged thorn of something done in haste.

depicts.m: Let the moth fall into the blazing flame not knowing that it burns; let the fish swallow the bait not knowing the hook. But we, knowing full well, still do not let go of desires tangled in a net of dangers. Ah, how deep is the power of delusion!
depicts.sa: अजानन्दाहात्म्यं पततु शलभस्तीव्रदहने स मीनोऽप्यज्ञानाद्वडिशयुतमश्नातु पिशितम् । विजानन्तोऽप्येते वयमिह विपज्जालजटिलान् न मुञ्चामः कामानहह गहनो मोहमहिमा ॥

depicts.m: If the rain does not favour him, the farmer is not to blame. He tells himself: 'Whatever anyone could have done, I have done.' If the result is still this, the fault is not mine. Seeing this, the wise do not condemn themselves.
depicts.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
depicts.sa: वृष्टिश्चेन्नानुगृह्णीयादनेनास्तत्र कर्षकः / यदन्यः पुरुषः कुर्यात्तत्कृतं सफलं मया तच्चेदं फलमस्माकमपराधो न मे क्वचित् / इति धीरोऽन्ववेक्ष्यैव नात्मानं तत्रगर्हयेत्
depicts.why: Speaks to the one asking whether a failed result was their own doing.

depicts.m: Remembering what she had done, her heart was full of a worry beyond telling. 'Shiva, an ocean of compassion, deep beyond measure, did not speak my fault aloud.'
depicts.sa: हृदयँ सोचु समुझत निज करनी। चिंता अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ कृपासिंधु सिव परम अगाधा। प्रगट न कहेउ मोर अपराधा ॥
depicts.why: Shows her knowing it as her own offence.

depicts.m: It was as if his mother's wrong held him back, while the strength of devotion drove him on like a patient ox. Whenever he remembered Raghunath's nature, his feet moved faster on the path.
depicts.sa: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥
depicts.why: Shows his feet pulled back by a wrong that was not his.

depicts.m: Whether out of grief, love or childishness, I came here against your will. Even then, kind one, you looked at it from your own side and took everything I did as good.
depicts.sa: सोक सनेहँ कि बाल सुभाएँ। आयउँ लाइ रजायसु बाएँ॥ तबहुँ कृपाल हेरि निज ओरा। सबहि भाँति भल मानेउ मोरा ॥
depicts.why: Shows him admitting he came against the order.

depicts.m: My Lord, do not hold my faults in your mind. Your name is "the one who sees all alike"; live up to it and carry me across. One piece of iron is kept in the shrine for worship, another lies in a butcher's house; the touchstone knows no such difference, and turns both into pure gold.
depicts.sa: हमारे प्रभु, औगुन चित न धरो । समदरसी है नाम तुम्हारा, सोई पार करौ॥ इक लोहा पूजा में राखत, इक घर बधिक परो। सो दुबिधा पारस नहिं जानत, कंचन करत खरो॥

depicts.m: Till now it has been wasted; from now it will not be. By Ram's grace the long night is over. Now that I am awake, I will not spread the bed of sleep again.
depicts.sa: अबलों नसानी, अब न नसैहौं। राम-कृपा भव-निसा सिरानी, जागे फिरि न डसैहौं॥
depicts.why: Depicts the years till now were lost.

gloss: In the Manas this is Bharat's glāni. The Upanishad names the thought itself: 'why did I not do right, why did I do wrong?'

heals.m: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
heals.sa: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
heals.why: Shows a person being their own friend, not their own prosecutor.

heals.m: One who feels remorse for a wrong deed is freed from that wrong; by resolving 'I will not do it again', he is freed from the second.
heals.sa: विकर्मणा तप्यमानः पापाद्विपरिमुच्यते / न तत्कुर्यां पुनरिति द्वितीयात्परिमुच्यते
heals.why: Gives remorse a job and an end point.

heals.m: If the rain does not favour him, the farmer is not to blame. He tells himself: 'Whatever anyone could have done, I have done.' If the result is still this, the fault is not mine. Seeing this, the wise do not condemn themselves.
heals.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
heals.sa: वृष्टिश्चेन्नानुगृह्णीयादनेनास्तत्र कर्षकः / यदन्यः पुरुषः कुर्यात्तत्कृतं सफलं मया तच्चेदं फलमस्माकमपराधो न मे क्वचित् / इति धीरोऽन्ववेक्ष्यैव नात्मानं तत्रगर्हयेत्
heals.why: Shows separating what was in one's hands from what was not.

heals.m: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
heals.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
heals.sa: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना

heals.m: The Lord does not keep a mistake in his mind; he remembers the heart a hundred times over. The very wrong for which he struck Bali like a hunter, Sugriva later did too.
heals.sa: रहति न प्रभु चित चूक किए की। करत सुरति सय बार हिए की॥ जेहिं अघ बधेउ ब्याध जिमि बाली। फिरि सुकंठ सोइ कीन्हि कुचाली ॥
heals.why: Remembers the mistake is not what is remembered.

heals.m: Even such people, hearing of you, came before you for shelter, and with a single bow you made them your own. You saw their faults but never kept them in your heart; you heard their virtues and praised them among the good.
heals.sa: तेउ सुनि सरन सामुहें आए। सकृत प्रनामु किहें अपनाए॥ देखि दोष कबहुँ न उर आने। सुनि गुन साधु समाज बखाने ॥
heals.why: Shows faults are seen and not held.

heals.m: There is no doubt: past faults are calmed by present virtues. The proof is that yesterday's mistake is undone by today's good deeds.
heals.sa: दोषः शाम्यत्यसंदेहं प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनैर्गुणैः । दृष्टान्तोऽत्र ह्यस्तनस्य दोषस्याद्य गुणैः क्षयः ॥
heals.why: Shows a past mistake is not permanent.

heals.m: Hear once more my highest word, the most secret of all: you are deeply loved by me, and so I will tell you what is good for you.
heals.sa: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
heals.why: Shows the love declared before any condition is set.

hero.m: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
hero.sa: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥

loci.m: Such a one is no longer tormented by the thought: why did I not do good? Why did I do wrong?
loci.sa: एतꣳह वाव न तपति । किमहꣳसाधु नाकरवम् । किमहं पापमकरवमिति ।

loci.m: This sorrow has come to me, my queen, by my own doing, like a child who swallows poison out of ignorance.
loci.sa: तदिदं मेऽनुसम्प्राप्तं देवि दुःखं स्वयंकृतम्। सम्मोहादिह बालेन यथा स्याद् भक्षितं विषम्॥

practices.m: Do your allotted work, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
practices.sa: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
practices.why: Shows settles the question of whether to act at all.

practices.m: One who, by comparison with himself, sees the same everywhere, Arjuna, whether in pleasure or in pain, is considered the highest yogi.
practices.sa: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥
practices.why: Shows others' pain is known by one's own.

practices.m: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
practices.sa: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
practices.why: Shows the decision to be on one's own side.

practices.m: The lowest do not begin at all, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
practices.sa: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥

practices.m: The ear is beautiful through learning, not earrings; the hand through giving, not bracelets; the body of the compassionate shines through helping others, not through sandal paste.
practices.sa: श्रोत्रं श्रुतेनैव न कुण्डलेन दानेन पाणिर्न तु कङ्कणेन । विभाति कायः करुणापराणां परोपकारैर्न तु चन्दनेन ॥

practices.m: Cut off craving, practise forbearance, give up arrogance, take no delight in wrong, speak the truth, follow the path of the good, serve the wise, honour those worthy of honour, win over even your enemies, show courtesy, guard your good name, be kind to those in pain: this is how the good behave.
practices.sa: तृष्णां छिन्धि भज क्षमां जहि मदं पापे रतिं मा कृथाः सत्यं ब्रूह्यनुयाहि साधुपदवीं सेवस्व विद्वज्जनम् । मान्यान् मानय विद्विषोऽप्यनुनय प्रख्यापय प्रश्रयं कीर्तिं पालय दुःखिते कुरु दयामेतत् सतां चेष्टितम् ॥
practices.why: Cultivates kindness to those in pain.

practices.m: Ocean of compassion, Ganapati: may your radiance, which the whole world worships, by its own power quickly guard our minds, day and night, from wrong action, and urge them to good action. Blessed one, with Siddhi at your left side, we bow to you.
practices.sa: भर्गो विश्वसमर्चितं यदिह ते ह्यास्ते दयासागर ! तन्नो बुद्धिमहर्निशं गणपते ! शक्तचा स्वया सत्वरम । संरक्ष्यासत एव कर्मनिवहात् सत्कर्मणि प्रेरयेत् सियाऽलङ्कृतवामपार्श्व ! भगवस्त्वां सन्नमामो वयमा ॥

practices.m: Do not wound others where it hurts, do not speak cruelly, do not take from those who have less. Never say words that make another person flinch; such words are scorching and lead to dark places.
practices.sa: नारुतुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादी / न हीनतः परमभ्याददीत / ययाऽस्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत / न तां वदेदुशतिं पापलोक्याम्
practices.why: Shows one feeling the other's flinch before speaking.

stories.l: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.
stories.s: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.

stories.l: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.
stories.s: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.

stories.l: Where you start is not where you end; you can be taken in from nothing.
stories.s: Across his later works Tulsidas tells his own story: left by his parents at birth, he wandered door to door for scraps, no job, no trade, no skill, ignored by everyone. Good people told him not to worry; Hanuman raised him like a child; Ram's name, he says, turned a thorny babul into a mango tree. Even when he went astray, he was taken back.
stories.t: Tulsidas, the boy who begged for scraps

stories.l: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.
stories.s: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.
stories.t: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage
